test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 9 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My granny says that / it is quite right / to get married young, / though I do not absolute agree with her a bit on this.

options.text: though I do not absolute agree with her a bit on this

solution:
The correct answer will be **"though I do not absolute agree with her a bit on this"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is divided into four parts. Among them one part is incorrect.
 
• In the last part, "**agree"** is a **verb**. Because of this, "**absolute"** will be an adverb before "**agree"**.
 
• **Adverbs** are used to provide additional details about a verb.
 
• We should use **"absolutely" **before "agree" that the sentence will be correct.

The correct sentence is **"My granny says that it is quite right to get married young, though I do not absolutely agree with her a bit on this."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other parts of the given sentence are **grammatically **correct.
 
• **Adverbs** function as modifiers for verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs in English grammar. Adverbs and **adverbial phrases** frequently serve the purpose of describing the how, when, and where of events.
 
• If We do question how i agree, we will get answer **"absolutely"** as because this is used before verb **"agree"**.
